A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEAR study. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPEAR evaluations and ablations on ALFWorld, WebShop, AIME 2024/2025 and Sokoban, alongside behavioral and runtime analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds search-augmented QA results and further behavioral analyses.

M1.justification: Replay filtering, median-based advantage recalibration, curriculum schedules, covariance clipping and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. Their relocation and condensed descriptions do not establish a changed SPEAR procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 adds knowledge-intensive search QA across NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue and Bamboogle. This substantially extends task coverage beyond the retained embodied, shopping, mathematical reasoning and Sokoban tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds Search-R1 as an evaluated comparator. It removes GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Pro rows from Table 1 and the Qwen2.5-Math, Sky-T1, o1-preview, DeepSeek-R1-Qwen, QwQ variants and s1 rows from Table 2. Their continued mention in Appendix A.11 does not retain those reported comparisons.

E3.justification: New QA experiments use Qwen2.5-7B/14B, local wiki-18 retrieval with HNSW indexing and a 32-turn limit. Table 8 also revises the math actor minibatch from 64 to 32 and maximum turns from 8 to 8/15. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.14 adds context-budget analyses of response lengths and tool calls, paired AIME reasoning examples, entropy trajectories across tasks and model sizes, and a 50-sample manual check of automated intent labels. Existing component ablations and Figure 7 sensitivity results are retained.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly labels the AIME ablations in Table 4 as mean@30; v3 omits that designation, although Table 2 retains it. This is a limited loss of repeated-sampling information, not evidence of fewer runs. No new training-seed, confidence-interval or significance-test reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Retained entries in Tables 1–4 and the Sokoban comparison are unchanged. New QA results include 7B HotpotQA scores of 46.9 for SPEAR versus 37.0 for Search-R1, but lower NQ scores of 35.7 versus 39.3. Table 9 and Figure 13 add behavioral and entropy results; several earlier baseline result rows are removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.9 introduces four claims and associated theorems/proofs concerning surrogate improvement, median robustness, minimax estimation and dual filtering. v1 contains the algorithmic equations and complexity analysis but no corresponding guarantees. These additions substantially expand the formal content, irrespective of their validity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the curriculum-guided self-imitation contribution, Dr.BoT baseline, plug-and-play applicability and the same headline performance and overhead claims. Condensing the contribution list does not materially change their meaning.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of search-based decomposition, model-specific context-budget behavior and the imperfect relationship between exploration and entropy. Appendix A.16 develops dynamic scheduling and stepwise credit-assignment proposals. Conversely, v1's explicit warning that AIME baselines differ in training data, frameworks and hyperparameters is removed.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promise of forthcoming resources with code and checkpoint links. It adds QA configuration details, 96GB GPU-memory disclosure, hyperparameter-tuning guidance, the intent-classification workflow and an explanation of gradient accumulation and memory usage. These substantially expand the documented reproduction guidance.

R1.justification: v3 expands connections to QA/retrieval research, robust statistics, off-policy theory, implicit process rewards and world models, particularly in Appendices A.9 and A.16. It removes the GSPO and mixture-of-experts discussion and citations while retaining the central positioning relative to SIL and exploration methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively condensed and rewritten. Action-space definitions, optimization background, reward details and several analyses move into a reorganized appendix, with new summaries, subsections and future-work discussion.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned; earlier Figures 4 and 6 are combined into v3 Figure 6. Numerous displays are resized and relocated, comparison tables lose baseline blocks, and Table 8 gains a QA column. New QA and context-budget tables, reasoning examples and entropy panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful QA coverage, diagnostic analyses and reproduction guidance. However, Figure 13(b) and 13(f) reuse an identical plot under ALFWorld and WebShop labels, while new Appendix A.9 Proof 4 asserts guarantees using a qualitative variance argument and an undefined Equation 39. These reliability problems materially counterbalance the additions, leaving the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
